reason: This passage (Exodus 14) focuses on God's deliverance of Israel from Egypt and the parting of the Red Sea. The central themes are God's mighty acts, His demonstration of power over Pharaoh, and making His identity known to the Egyptians (וְיָדְע֥וּ מִצְרַ֖יִם כִּֽי־ אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה - 'Egypt will know that I am Yahweh'). The text contains no mention of worship, sacrifice, offerings, or proper religious practices. The statement, while applicable to other portions of the Hebrew Bible (such as Leviticus or passages dealing with sacrificial law), does not characterize the concerns expressed in this specific narrative.
